newsitem.title: INDIA: India's RBI buys spot dlr, forwards volatile.
newsitem.headline: India's RBI buys spot dlr, forwards volatile.

text.p: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) bought spot dollars late afternoon trade Tuesday at 35.715/720 rupees to prevent the Indian currency's rise, dealers said.
"They bought at 35.715 to 35.720," said a bank dealer.
Premiums in the forward dollar market were erratic, but continued the general uptrend seen since Monday, dealers said.
"July premiums touched a high of 2.07 rupees but have fallen now to 1.93/1.96 rupees," a leading forex broker said.
"I haven't seen any major corporate covering this week," said a dealer at a foreign bank.

"Many banks are cutting their huge received positions after Reddy's speech at Goa," a bank dealer said, referring to the RBI deputy governor's comment at a weekend forex dealers' conference that the rupee appeared to be overvalued.
Dealers said several banks, which normally keep their foreign currency deposits in dollars have begun swapping them into rupees after the deputy governor's speech.
This could be an indication that a correction of the overvalued rupee was in the offing, they said.
